stem: The artist famous for blending European academic realism with Indian themes, especially in oil paintings of gods and epics, was __________.
solution: Raja Ravi Varma blended Western academic oil technique with Indian mythological subjects.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma made his art widely available to the public through __________.
solution: Ravi Varma's oleograph prints made his images of gods popular in ordinary homes.

stem: The group of modern Indian artists formed in Bombay in 1947 was the __________.
solution: The Progressive Artists' Group was formed in Bombay in 1947.

stem: A founding member of the Progressive Artists' Group known for horses and bold lines was __________.
solution: M. F. Husain, famous for his horses, was a founding member of the Progressive Artists' Group.

stem: The artist S. H. Raza is known for his central motif, the __________.
solution: S. H. Raza is known for the 'Bindu', a central point symbolising the source of energy.

stem: The pioneering woman modernist who blended Western training with Indian subjects was __________.
solution: Amrita Sher-Gil was a pioneering modernist who fused Western technique with Indian subjects.

stem: Amrita Sher-Gil is especially remembered for her sympathetic portrayals of __________.
options: ordinary Indian village people, especially women
solution: Amrita Sher-Gil sympathetically portrayed ordinary Indian villagers, especially women.

stem: The artist who developed a distinctive flat, folk-inspired style based on Kalighat painting was __________.
solution: Jamini Roy developed a flat, bold style inspired by Bengal folk (Kalighat) art.

stem: The poet Rabindranath Tagore was also a notable modern Indian __________.
solution: Rabindranath Tagore was also a notable modern painter.

stem: The pioneering modern Indian sculptor known for works like 'Santhal Family' was __________.
solution: Ramkinkar Baij, a pioneer of modern Indian sculpture, made 'Santhal Family'.

stem: The Progressive Artists' Group aimed to create art that was __________.
options: modern and international yet rooted in India
solution: The Progressives sought a modern, international idiom rooted in Indian experience.

stem: The founding members of the Progressive Artists' Group included Husain, Raza, Souza and __________.
solution: K. H. Ara, along with S. K. Bakre and H. A. Gade, was a founder alongside Husain, Raza and Souza.

stem: F. N. Souza, a leading modernist, was known for his __________ style.
solution: F. N. Souza was known for a bold, expressionist, often distorted style.

stem: Modern Indian art after independence sought to break away from both __________.
options: colonial academic realism and pure revivalism
solution: Post-independence artists broke away from both colonial academic art and pure revivalism.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma belonged to the royal family of __________.
solution: Raja Ravi Varma belonged to the Travancore royal family of Kerala.

stem: Amrita Sher-Gil was influenced early by __________ art before turning to Indian themes.
solution: Amrita Sher-Gil trained in European (Paris) modernism before embracing Indian subjects.

stem: Jamini Roy deliberately rejected __________ to embrace an Indian folk idiom.
solution: Jamini Roy rejected Western academic oil painting for a simple Indian folk idiom.

stem: The modern Indian art movement is characterised by __________.
solution: Modern Indian art is marked by experimentation and diverse individual styles.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma's oleographs made images of Hindu deities __________.
solution: His mass-produced oleographs brought images of deities to ordinary homes.

stem: The 'Bindu' of S. H. Raza symbolises the __________.
solution: Raza's Bindu symbolises the source and centre of creation and energy.

stem: M. F. Husain is often called the '__________ of India'.
solution: M. F. Husain has been called the 'Picasso of India'.

stem: Modern Indian sculpture pioneers like Ramkinkar Baij used unconventional materials such as __________.
solution: Ramkinkar Baij pioneered the use of cement and laterite concrete in Indian sculpture.

stem: Rabindranath Tagore's paintings are noted for their __________ quality.
solution: Rabindranath Tagore's paintings are spontaneous and expressive.

stem: The theme of the common Indian person became central to the art of __________.
solution: Amrita Sher-Gil centred her art on the common Indian person, especially villagers.

stem: The Progressive Artists' Group was formed in the year __________.
solution: The Progressive Artists' Group was formed in 1947, the year of independence.

stem: Modern Indian artists drew inspiration from Indian folk and __________ art as well as global movements.
solution: Modern Indian artists drew on Indian folk and tribal art alongside global modernism.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma's famous subjects included scenes from the __________.
solution: Ravi Varma painted scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

stem: The modernist art of India after 1947 reflected the __________ of a newly independent nation.
solution: Post-1947 modernism reflected the aspirations and identity of a newly independent India.

stem: Jamini Roy's paintings are marked by __________.
options: bold flat colours and simple sweeping lines
solution: Jamini Roy's works have bold flat colours and simple, sweeping folk-style lines.

stem: The modern movement encouraged Indian artists to develop __________ styles.
solution: The modern movement encouraged individual, experimental styles.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma is regarded as one of the first Indian artists to master __________.
solution: Ravi Varma mastered the European oil painting technique.

stem: Modern Indian art includes both __________ and figurative works.
solution: Modern Indian art includes both abstract and figurative works.

stem: The Progressive Artists' Group was based in the city of __________.
solution: The Progressive Artists' Group was based in Bombay.

stem: The modern Indian artists engaged with global movements such as __________.
solution: Modern Indian artists engaged with Cubism, Expressionism and other global movements.

stem: The art of Amrita Sher-Gil combined the influence of __________.
options: Western modernism and Indian miniature/mural traditions
solution: Sher-Gil fused Western modernism with Indian miniature and mural influences.

stem: Modern Indian sculpture broke from tradition by exploring __________ forms and materials.
solution: Modern sculptors explored new, including abstract, forms and materials.

stem: The oleographs of Raja Ravi Varma played a role in __________ Indian visual culture.
options: popularising and standardising images of deities in
solution: His prints popularised and standardised images of deities in Indian visual culture.

stem: The modern period saw Indian art become part of the __________ art scene.
solution: Modern Indian art became part of the international art scene.

stem: The horses of M. F. Husain became a __________ of his artistic identity.
solution: Husain's dynamic horses became a signature motif of his art.

stem: Modern Indian art draws strength from India's __________ heritage and contemporary experience.
solution: Modern Indian art draws on India's rich traditional heritage and modern experience.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma won international recognition, including at __________ exhibitions.
solution: Ravi Varma won recognition at international (European) exhibitions.

stem: The modernists rejected the __________ that revivalists had emphasised.
solution: The modernists rejected the revivalist insistence on a strict return to the past.

stem: Modern Indian art is significant because it expresses a __________ identity.
solution: Modern Indian art expresses a distinct modern Indian identity.

stem: Raja Ravi Varma bridged __________ and popular taste.
solution: Ravi Varma bridged fine art and popular taste through his accessible images.

stem: The variety of modern Indian art reflects the __________ of modern India.
solution: The variety of modern Indian art reflects the diversity and dynamism of modern India.

stem: Jamini Roy sought to make art that was __________ and rooted in Indian tradition.
solution: Jamini Roy sought art that was simple, accessible and rooted in Indian folk tradition.

stem: The modern Indian artists valued __________ over blind imitation.
solution: Modern Indian artists valued creative freedom and experimentation.

stem: The transition from Raja Ravi Varma to the Progressives shows the movement of Indian art towards __________.
solution: The shift from Ravi Varma to the Progressives shows Indian art moving towards modernism.

stem: Modern Indian art is best described as __________.
options: diverse, experimental and rooted in national identity
solution: Modern Indian art is diverse, experimental and rooted in national identity.

stem: The overall achievement of modern Indian art is bringing India into a __________ dialogue while retaining its roots.
solution: Modern Indian art brought India into a global artistic dialogue while keeping its roots.
